Q: Render-looping when child and parent components both store state simultaneously A:

The main issue comes from having two sources of truth (states in both parent and child), which leads to render loops.

The recommended approach is to use a single source of truth, usually in the parent component, and pass data down via props while handling updates through callbacks.

For reusable components, a hybrid (controlled/uncontrolled) pattern can be used:

- If the parent provides values (props), the component behaves as a controlled component.

- If no values are provided, the component manages its own internal state.

However, both should not control the same state at the same time, as it leads to synchronization issues and infinite loops.

Q: git reset --hard HEAD leaves untracked files behind A:

git-clean Use to remove untracked files in the working tree. Following are some options (in brief) that can use with git clean command.

-d use when no path is specified. So git recurse into untracked directories remove them.

-f/--force To remove nested untracked files.

-i/--interactive Show what would be done and clean files interactively.

-n/--dry-run Show what will happen without removing anything.

-x Remove ignored files as well.

example: git clean -f -d -> Remove all untracked files in current directory any subdirectories.

Q: How to debug Firebase on iOS AdHoc build A:

The solution is here: https://github.com/firebase/firebase-ios-sdk/issues/14182#issuecomment-2535843927

UserDefaults.standard.set(true, forKey: "/google/firebase/debug_mode")
UserDefaults.standard.set(true, forKey: "/google/measurement/debug_mode")

This workaround is actually working, but only on the second launch of the app, so apparently the first launch does not recognize the UserDefaults value.

Q: Is calling S3 methods in my own S3 method a good idea? A:

I agree with @user2554330 that the best approach is to use your package's NAMESPACE file to manage your package's dependencies. Not least because that means that R will manage the dependencies when your package is installed. I find the easiest way to do this is with the usethis package. For example:

usethis::use_package("lme4")

It also removes the need to add a call to requireNamespace in every one of your package's functions that calls a third-party function. (I believe that using requireNamespace in this way is bad practice.)

Also, it's less than ideal to use ::: to access functions in other packages that are not exported. Package authors will have a reason for not exporting them, perhaps because they are not as stable as their published functions, perhaps because they envisiage changes in the future. Making your package depend on their private functions makes your package more fragile.

If there's a way to implement the functionality you need without resorting to use of another package's internal functions, I would take it. If not, then a potentially more robust way to "use" the internal function is to copy its source code to your package and then call that version in your code. That at least stabilises the code you use, though it doesn't protect you against future changes to calls to the internal function in exported functions in the third party package. (If you do this, I think you should document the source of copied code in your package's documentation.)

A good, long-term, potential solution is to write to the other package's authors, asking them to export the function you need. Explain youir reasons. Perhaps they will agree.

In case you haven't found it already, I believe Hadley's book on R packages is essential reading for package developers.
